data.title: Agencia Comercial Spirits says U.S. chip rules may affect AI computing rollout
data.description:
• Agencia Comercial Spirits (AGCC) said that U.S. regulatory requirements on remote access to advanced semiconductors may affect the timing of its AI computing services and customer arrangements.
  • The company said it is reviewing an interim final rule published November 19 by the U.S. Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security.
  • Agencia said its planned data center business will offer colocation and AI computing services. It clarified that it does not sell or resell semiconductor chips, hardware or servers to customers.
  • The company expects to begin AI computing services once its contracted computing capacity is available, subject to regulatory requirements.
  • The company also said that its AI computing and data center operations remain under development and that its historical operating revenue comes from its whisky business.
  • The stock price traded about 1.5% higher on Friday pre-market hours.

data.title: Bayer to invest up to €500M in Beijing site, its largest pharma investment in China to date
data.description:
• Bayer (BAYRY) on Friday announced plans to expand its Pharmaceuticals Product Supply Center in Beijing at a cost of up to €500M, the company’s single largest pharmaceutical investment in China to date.
  • Once complete, the site in the Beijing Economic-Technological Development Area will support the production of Bayer’s (BAYZF) cardiovascular drugs and future oncology products mainly for Chinese consumers, the company said.
  • The new plant will be built on Bayer’s (BAYRY) existing pharmaceutical manufacturing site in Beijing, and it is expected to begin production in 2032, accommodating up to 300 employees, the German conglomerate added. 
  • Since its operations at the Beijing Economic-Technological Development Area began in 1997, the company has expanded its pharma site there in 2006 and 2016, making the location its largest packaging facility for prescription drugs globally.

data.title: Altria's pursuit of Imperial Brands could have implications for Anheuser-Busch
data.description:
Imperial Brands (IMBBY) formally responded to reports of a potential acquisition offer from Altria (MO). The board said it has not had any discussions with, or received any approach or proposal from, Altria (MO).

The board noted that it is clear in its duty of aiming to maximize shareholder value and will consider any proposal, should one be made. Imperial Brands (IMBBY) said it has strong confidence in its strategy and trading.

On Wall Street, Citi analyst Simon Hales said a deal has considerable strategic logic for Altria (MO) since it could diversify its cigarette business geographically and add needed scale in next-generation products. While Citi expects no issues funding the transaction, funding the transaction could prompt Altria (MO) to lower or exit its roughly $12B stake in Anheuser-Busch InBev (BUD). Jefferies analyst Edward Mundy noted that if Anheuser-Busch InBev (BUD) absorbs the Altria (MO) stake, it would be high single-digit earnings accretive.

Shares of Imperial Brands (IMBBY) rose 6.6% in London trading on Friday. Altria (MO) was down 1.4%, and Anheuser-Busch InBev (BUD) showed a decline of 2.2%.

data.title: ECARX rises on $20M share buyback plan
data.description:
• Shares of London-based ECARX Holdings (ECX) are up ~9% on Friday after the company unveiled plans to buy back its ordinary shares of up to $20M by Nov. 30, 2027.
  • ECX expects to fund the repurchases out of its existing cash balance.
  • “This share repurchase authorization reflects our strong conviction that ECARX’s long-term value is not fully reflected in the current share price. This program demonstrates our confidence in ECARX's trajectory for sustainable long-term growth while continuing to focus on maximizing shareholder value,” said Dylan Jeng, ECX's CFO.

data.title: F4 Uranium to raise up to C$1.5M via flow-through financing
data.description:
F4 Uranium Corp. (FFUCF) has announced a non-brokered private placement of up to 17.65M  flow-through (FT) common shares priced at C$0.085 per share, targeting gross proceeds of up to approximately C$1.5M.

Proceeds will fund eligible Canadian exploration and critical mineral mining expenditures across F4 Uranium's Athabasca Basin projects in Saskatchewan by December 31, 2027, with all qualifying expenditures renounced to subscribers effective December 31, 2026.

The offering is expected to close around December 18, 2026, subject to TSX-V approval, the offering includes a four-month-and-one-day hold period and potential insider participation exempt from formal valuation and minority shareholder approval.

data.title: Black Friday: Shoppers hunt for deals as investors buy staples
data.description:
Sticky inflation and affordability concerns aren't deterring Americans from going shopping this year, but they're definitely putting pressure on wallets and pocketbooks. An estimated 182.7M people across the country are planning to shop in-store and online from Thanksgiving Day through Cyber Monday, according to the National Retail Federation, which is 4M people less than the record high notched last year. To keep budgets in check, many are taking steps to manage holiday costs, including buying less expensive gifts or cutting back in other areas.

Snapshot: Black Friday continues to be the most popular day to shop, with around 69% (126M people) planning to take advantage of deals. The NRF even forecasts that total holiday spending during November and December will surpass $1T for the first time, with sales predicted to grow 4.2% over 2025. The numbers highlight the resilience of the American consumer, which continues to bolster the U.S. economy.

"Holiday shopping continues to be pulled forward, but Thanksgiving weekend remains an important shopping event for consumers," noted Allison Zeller, NRF Vice President of Industry and Consumer Insights. "Shoppers are looking for deals, and retailers are delivering great value on gifts while creating special experiences that keep the Thanksgiving weekend shopping tradition going."

Stock returns: The investing side of retail reflects the budget-conscious dynamic, with defensive essentials outpacing discretionary splurges. Consumer Staples (XLP) has been a clear sector winner, gaining 4.1% over the past month, 10.4% over six months, and 18.2% over the past year. Standout YTD performers include big-box stores like Target (TGT) +76%, Costco (COST) +26% and Walmart (WMT) +18%, as well as consumer giants like Coca-Cola (KO) +40%, Colgate-Palmolive (CL) +26% and Procter & Gamble (PG) +21%. While an AI pullback and tariff uncertainty have slashed high-valuation growth exposure, capital has steadily rotated into businesses prized for low cyclicality, durable cash flows, and dependable dividends.
